title: Advanced Barbell
author: Iron And Sand
desc:
ADVANCED BARBELL

3x5 isn't dead. You're just ready for more.

When should you consider undertaking this program? 

I sold Essential Barbell as the only strength training program you need. And it is - but what we need and what we want don't always necessarily coincide.

First of all, if you haven't used Essential Barbell I'd advise you do so before trying this program.  Carry on using it.....until you literally can't. Then give Advanced Barbell a go.

You should adopt Advanced Barbell if:

1. You've plateaued with one or more lift for more than a month.
2. You're specifically seeking strength progression with the main four main lifts.
3. You're bored of 3x5 and it's affecting your will to train.

Advanced Barbell follows a 4-week cycle, each week consisting of 3 workouts. Ideally you will train with a rest day between workouts. 

Advanced Barbell utilises the exact same lifts as Essential Barbell, but follows different rep and set ranges to provide a novel stimulus for both body and mind. Nothing new is introduced; the same fundamental lifts are simply performed differently, with greater emphasis on strength development while also maintaining hypertrophy.

I alternate 3x5 with 6x2-3 for the squat and presses, to allow strength-specific focus while encouraging continued muscle growth.  
For a 6x 2-3 workout you will begin lifting a weight for 6 sets of 2 reps.  Each workout you will add ONE SINGLE REP in the following manner:

6x2.
5x2, 1x3.
4x2, 2x3.
3x2, 3x3.
2x2, 4x3.
1x2, 5x3.
6x3.

When you achieve 6x3 with good form, you can increase the weight the next time you workout and begin again with 6x2.  
This very strict and regimented way of progression provides sustainable and repeated exposure at a high weight, allowing time for the whole body to adapt to the increasing workload, rather than relying solely on muscular adaptation.

I"ve prioritised overhead press for maximal strength development using this method. However, you may prefer to prioritise bench press. If so, simply apply the 6×2–3 progression to bench press instead of OHP. You could theoretically apply it to both, but I suspect for most lifters this will compromise progress on at least one of these lifts.

The deadlift is programmed once a week, and I have prescribed 6x2-3 FOLLOWED by 3 sets of 6-8.  The 3x6-8 works in the same way.....

3x6.
2x6, 1x7.
1x6, 2x7.
3x7.
2x7, 1x8.
1x7, 2x8.
3x8.

This is a lot of stress on the body and you may want to take an additional rest day after this workout. However I found this preferable to alternating heavy and volume deadlift each week, because alternating the two makes progression on the heavy work unnecessarily slow for what is actually a very strong lift.  You can do either, but if deadlift strength is a priority I prefer combining the heavy and volume work in the same session.  
The aim isn't to turn these into another heavy progression; it's to accumulate quality volume after the main strength work.

Preferably use overhand or neutral grip as this will increase lat engagement. Underarm 'chins' will focus on biceps.
If you want to you can rotate the grip you use, every 6 weeks or so.
If you don't have a dipping belt you can suspend weight plates, kettlebells or a dumbbell from a tight resistance band. Its unwieldy but it works. You can also use a small rucksack or weighted vest.
